name: Ad network retargeting audiences
plain: Ad pixels add a visitor to lists the site owner can later target with ads elsewhere.
meaning: A tag fires on page load or product view and adds a cookie or hashed email to an audience (for example Meta Custom Audiences, Google remarketing lists, LinkedIn Matched Audiences). Windows run up to 180 days at Meta and 540 days at Google Ads.

web.api: Meta Pixel fbq('track', ...), Google tag gtag('event', ...), LinkedIn Insight Tag, server APIs

access.persistence: Membership windows set per audience: Meta up to 180 days, Google Ads up to 540 days
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can add you to an ad list when you visit a site, so ads follow you
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you visit a site with an ad pixel
can: Add you to a list tied to your visit
Let the site owner target you with ads on other platforms
Use pages you viewed or items you added to a cart as the trigger
cannot: Add you if the pixel is blocked
Show ads if you opt out of personalized ads
Work between browsers or devices unless a login links them
Name you; the owner sees only the list size
limits.reach_label: A list built from your visits
limits.differs: Safari and Firefox limit pixel cookies. Chrome allows them.

story.what_it_is: Ad pixels add you to lists so the site's owner can show you ads elsewhere.

marketing.name: Custom Audiences
marketing.pitch: Meta pitches it as a way to reach people who visited your site or are in your lists with ads.

story.for_you: You look at a product, then see that product in ads for days. A pixel put you in a list. The list can last 180 days on Meta and 540 on Google Ads.
story.for_makers: People who already showed interest buy more often than strangers. Retargeting lists turn visits into a cheap ad audience. They are one of the main reasons sites run ad pixels.

use_cases.example: You leave a pair of shoes in the cart and see them on Instagram all week.
Google remarketing follows you with display ads for the same product for weeks.
A game website retargets people who visited the store page but did not buy, with a sale ad.
You search for flights, and ads for that route follow you around.
A software firm shows case studies to people who visited the pricing page.
A subscription site shows you a deal after you hit its paywall.

risks: Based on pages you thought were private

technical_bounds: Platforms require minimum audience sizes before serving (about 100 to 1000 matched users, varies by product)
Needs the person to be recognisable (cookie, click ID or hashed email)
Consent rules (GDPR, ePrivacy) apply to the tags in the EU

abuse: Following a person across sites and apps after a single visit

linkedin.how: LinkedIn Insight Tag and its ad stack use this technique on advertiser sites (see research/linkedin-case.md).

history.change: Google Consent Mode v2 required for EEA remarketing audiences
Privacy Sandbox Protected Audience, the in-browser retargeting alternative, retired
